concept_options.title: Beat-Locked Material Reel
concept_options.hook: Herringbone, veined quartz, brass — one house, 45 seconds, every cut on the kick.
concept_options.visual_approach: The user's own sequence, compressed to the track's measured 114 BPM bar grid: 4 bars of plucks on the exterior, hard drop into the kitchen at 0:08.4, one-bar holds on both kick dropouts, tightest cutting on the lower level, deck sweep into the logo. Wides land on downbeats, material detail inserts on off-beats.
concept_options.target_audience: North Jersey homeowners evaluating a custom builder
key_points: Every room in the brief appears, weighted by how much material story it carries
Cut rhythm is derived from the track's real grid, not an eyeballed pace
The listing address is masked so the piece works as a builder brand asset
concept_options.core_message: WA Construct finishes a home to a level you can see in a half-second insert.
concept_options.why_this_works: The measured structure gives exactly the shape the brief asks for inside 45s: a pluck intro, a drop, two engineered breaths, and a lift under the logo. Nothing has to be faked with dissolves.

concept_options.title: Detail-First Cold Open
concept_options.hook: Start on brass. Pull back and the whole house is already yours.
concept_options.visual_approach: Invert the brief: open on three tight material inserts (brass tap, quartz vein, herringbone grain) during the plucks, and hold the exterior reveal for the drop at 0:08.4. The house is then toured in the same order, but every section opens on a detail and resolves to the room wide.
key_points: The exterior reveal becomes a payoff instead of an establishing shot
Denser detail coverage than a standard tour reel
concept_options.core_message: This is a builder whose details survive a close-up.
concept_options.why_this_works: The research landscape shows room-wide tours are saturated; leading on material is the underserved gap. Risk: it delays the property context by 8 seconds, which can cost feed retention.

concept_options.title: Two-Half Split — Light Then Dark
concept_options.hook: Upstairs is white oak and skylight. Downstairs is dark quartz and blue onyx.
concept_options.visual_approach: Reorder the tour into two contrasting movements: everything light (exterior, kitchen, bedrooms, primary suite) across the first drop section, then a hard tonal flip at the 0:40 break into the dark lower level — secondary kitchen, brass domes, blue onyx bath — with the deck and logo closing outside.
concept_options.target_audience: Buyers who want to see range in one property
key_points: Palette contrast carries the structure instead of floor-by-floor order
The lower level gets real weight rather than a single bar
One hard tonal flip is more memorable than eight even cuts
concept_options.core_message: One build, two completely different moods.
concept_options.why_this_works: Uses the second kick dropout as a palette pivot rather than a breath. Risk: it departs from the sequential room order the brief specified, and the deck outro has to share the last bar with the flip.

selected_concept.rationale: The brief already specifies the room order and the emotional shape; c1 delivers exactly that against the track's measured grid rather than re-inventing the direction. c2 and c3 are offered as real alternatives if the user wants a stronger creative departure.
modifications: Compressed from the brief's 1:39 timeline to 45s: the primary suite drops from 11s to 6.3s and the lower level from 19s to 2.1s
Cut grid rebuilt on the track's measured 114 BPM instead of the assumed 120 BPM

tools.role: Find the source's own shot boundaries so cuts never land mid-whip-pan

stages.approach: Convert the beat map into a shot list: for each of the 30-ish slots, name the source timecode range that fills it. Requires the source file.
stages.fallback_if_unavailable: Manual scrub via frame_sampler if scene detection under-segments a long gimbal take

tools.role: Pull candidate frames at each detected boundary to pick the strongest in/out points
tools.why_this_provider: Local frame extraction, no API cost

stages.approach: Lock in/out timecodes per slot against the beat grid; verify each slot's content matches the brief's room order and material callouts.
stages.fallback_if_unavailable: Sample on a fixed interval instead of at boundaries

tools.role: Cut the 30-ish segments from the source at frame accuracy
Already run — supplied the loudness profile and window choice

stages.approach: Trim segments, build the address mask plate for the intro, prepare the logo lockup asset.
Write edit_decisions: the cut list with music-locked in/out times, the address mask (blur or crop), the deck fade-to-plate, and the logo overlay timing.

tools.role: Assemble the cut, mask, fade, logo overlay and music mix
tools.why_this_provider: Source-footage concat with overlays is exactly ffmpeg's job; no synthetic scenes are needed

tools.role: Mix the music bed, set the level, fade out over the final 1.5s
Single consistent grade pass across all segments
tools.why_this_provider: Keeps interior/exterior white balance from jumping cut to cut

stages.approach: Render 45.0s at the source frame rate, H.264, then verify duration and cut positions against the beat grid.
stages.fallback_if_unavailable: If the user picks Remotion instead, route through OffthreadVideo scenes

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: FFmpeg direct cut vs Remotion re-composition of the footage
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: FFmpeg cuts the original frames with one grade pass — no browser re-render of 4K footage, no generational quality loss, and far faster. Remotion would only pay off if the reel needed animated title cards or motion-graphic overlays, which this brief does not.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Address burn-in: blur/mask patch vs crop-in
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Decide after seeing the frame — crop-in if the text sits near an edge, patch-blur if it sits over detail
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: Crop-in loses a little framing; a patch reads cleanly if the background behind the text is even
The lower level compresses to a single bar of fast hits; if that section matters commercially, a 60s cut would give it a full 4 bars

line_items.operation: Scene detect, trim, mask, grade, overlay, mix, render
line_items.notes: Every tool in this plan is local — no API providers are configured or needed for a footage-led cut

approval.user_notes: Blocked pending: (1) a retrievable copy of the source footage, (2) the WA Construct logo as a file, (3) confirmation of aspect ratio, (4) confirmation of render runtime (ffmpeg recommended; Remotion is being installed so it is a live option).

beat_map.why_this_window: Starts 4 bars before the track's main drop (33.168s) so the reel opens on plucks and drops at 0:08.4; the track's one-bar kick dropouts at 47.905s and 64.747s land at 0:23.2 and 0:40.0 in reel time, giving a free breath before the primary suite and again under the deck/logo outro.

sections.name: Intro — plucks
sections.cut_unit: 1 bar (2.11s), last bar split to 2 half-bars
sections.content: Exterior facade with the red maple, push to front door, entry with light-oak herringbone, iron-spindle staircase
sections.notes: Address burn-in ('271 Springfield Ave, Paramus NJ 07652') masked across the whole 0-6s source region it occupies

sections.name: Drop — chef's kitchen
sections.content: Open-concept wide on the drop, white shaker cabinets, quartz island with bold gray veining, unlacquered brass hardware inserts
sections.notes: First cut lands exactly on the kick at music 33.168s

sections.name: Break bar — move upstairs
sections.notes: Track pulls its kick for this bar (music 47.905s) — the hold is what makes the re-entry read

sections.name: Bedrooms & utility
sections.content: Wide-plank rift-sawn oak, bright secondary bedrooms, marble-tiled guest bath, black-and-white checkered laundry
sections.notes: Checkered laundry cuts last — highest contrast hit of the section

sections.name: Primary suite — slower
sections.content: Freestanding soaking tub under the skylight, book-matched marble walk-in shower, dual vanity with arched gold mirrors
sections.notes: Pacing halves against the kitchen while the music stays up — the contrast is the point

sections.name: Lower level — fast sweeps
sections.content: Secondary kitchen, dark quartz counters, brass dome pendants, blue onyx bath
sections.notes: Four hits in one bar — the tightest cutting in the reel

sections.name: Break bar — deck
sections.content: Stabilized sweep across the elevated composite deck and backyard
sections.notes: Second kick dropout (music 64.747s) — the deck gets the reel's only real breath

sections.name: Brand lockup
sections.content: Deck shot continues, fades to a semi-transparent plate, WA Construct logo resolves over it
sections.notes: Logo lands on the lift at music 66.852s; music fades out over the final 1.5s
